A1.justification: The complete 20-page v2 and 22-page v3 describe the same iiANET work and support comparison of their text, equations, tables, figures, and end matter. Neither contains a separately labeled appendix. V2's explicitly labeled BLANK figure panels are identifiable placeholders, not extraction failures.

before.justification: V2 reports original iiANET classification, COCO detection and instance-segmentation results, Grad-CAM visualizations, and component, head-size, channel-ratio, and register ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original base-model results and reports additional iiANET-L, ADE20K segmentation, spatial-transport, efficiency, and fusion-ablation outcomes.

M1.justification: V3 adds iiANET-L with stage depths [2,3,10,4], alongside the original [2,3,5,2] architecture renamed iiANET-B. The core convolution, r-MHSA, register, ECA, and concatenation/shuffling components remain. Table 9's 'additive fusion' label conflicts with the retained method description and does not establish a definite change to the base fusion procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds ADE20K semantic segmentation and a synthetic task transporting shapes between distant image regions. ImageNet-1K, AID, Oxford Pets, and COCO were already evaluated in v2. RLD remains represented in Grad-CAM evaluation despite removal of its quantitative classification rows.

E2.justification: Classification comparisons add methods including Vim-S, VMamba-T, DeiT-B, and Cross-ViT-B, while removing several existing entries, including EfficientNet-B4 and DenseNet-169. Instance-segmentation comparisons add PVT-L and CAE-GReaT. These change comparator membership within retained experiments; the COCO detection comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include 512×512 ADE20K segmentation with mIoU and a controlled 224×224 spatial-transport experiment using AdamW, learning rate 0.001, 50 epochs, and MSE loss. V3 also evaluates the larger variant, including 120 ImageNet training epochs. Its baseline-protocol statement changes from retraining the comparison models to mixing retrained models and published results; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds iiABlock-versus-MHSA profiling across channels, spatial resolutions, and attention heads (Table 6), fusion-strategy ablations (Table 9), and controlled spatial-transport cases (Figure 6). The original component ablation is retained, while head-size and register studies receive revised results and expanded analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added loss curves and result rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V3 adds iiANET-L results, including 84.9% ImageNet and 83.11% AID top-1 accuracy, and ADE20K mIoU of 48.5%/49.2% for B/L. It removes RLD classification and classification-throughput entries. The head ablation changes from 76.85% to 80.23%, with v3 specifying the last stage; zero/four-register results change from 80.57%/80.77% to 80.36%/80.57%. Retained base-model benchmark scores are unchanged, so the larger variant's scores are not same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.6 adds formal computational-cost expressions for attention, convolution branches, and register-augmented attention, including the assumption N much smaller than the spatial-token count. V3 also replaces v2's inconsistent intermediate channel-allocation algebra with a direct 1:6:1 allocation. No theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions centrally claim that iiABlock and iiANET efficiently combine local convolutional features with global attention to capture long-range dependencies and outperform some existing models. Rewritten contribution bullets and additional variant results do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V3 reverses the earlier interpretation that changing the channel ratio increases computational cost, instead describing an efficiency–accuracy tradeoff, and characterizes the head-size effect as small. It adds scaling/configuration difficulties as a limitation and explains small-dataset ViT underperformance through limited training data. The localized-object limitation remains, but its explicit ImageNet example is removed.

D1.justification: V3 adds dedicated ablation hardware/software information: RTX 2070 Max-Q, CUDA 12.1, and PyTorch 2.0. It specifies the last-stage scope of the head ablation and provides settings for the new transport experiment. Main training-system details remain unchanged. V2's explicit GitHub code link is removed, reducing access information without establishing that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V3 adds an ADRnet discussion and references supporting state-space-model comparisons, dense prediction, and gated fusion, including Vision Mamba, S4ND, and VMamba. The MobileNetV2 reference is removed. The main positioning around CNN, transformer, and hybrid-model limitations remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: V3 extensively edits and compresses related-work and method prose, reorganizes method subsections, and replaces the short quantitative discussion with dataset-specific and task-specific sections. Ablations receive structured explanations, and front matter and closing declarations change. Detection prose is aligned with YOLOv8, which was already named in v2's results table.

P2.justification: The paper is comprehensively retypeset with different typography, margins, headers, and table layouts. V3 adds a branch schematic table, dense-prediction examples, spatial-transport plots, and efficiency/fusion tables. Figure 4 is consolidated and its BLANK placeholders removed; classification tables are restructured without the throughput column or RLD block.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens evidence for long-range modeling through the controlled spatial-transport test and broadens evaluation with semantic segmentation, additional comparators, and efficiency analyses. It also corrects prose/table mismatches and removes unfinished figure placeholders. These gains are moderated by the new fusion-table inconsistency and removal of the code link. The net improvement rests on stronger supporting evidence and clearer reporting, not the larger variant's higher scores.
